How Sabbatical collects, uses and protects the details you share.
What we collect when you inquire, why, and what you can ask us to do with it.

Sabbatical plans tailor-made trips abroad: one- to six-month stays in a furnished home with a local host. Our address is Second Home Lisboa, Mercado da Ribeira, Avenida 24 de Julho 49, 1200-479 Lisboa, Portugal. We decide how the personal data described here is used and are responsible for it. Write to us about anything on this page at
what you send through our enquiry form or by email: names, email address, phone number if you give one, travel dates, group size and ages of children, interests, budget band and your message.

once you ask us to plan or book a trip, what is needed to arrange it, such as names as they appear in passports, dates of birth, arrival and departure details, dietary needs and, only if you choose to tell us, health or access needs.
if a newsletter sign-up is offered and you use it, your email address.
this site runs no analytics or advertising trackers.
We do not take payment card details through this site.
Why we use it, and on what basis
To answer your enquiry and prepare a proposal, because you asked us to (steps taken at your request before a contract).
To plan, book and run your trip (performance of our contract with you).
To handle health or access needs you tell us about, with your explicit consent, which you can withdraw at any time.
To keep the accounting and booking records the law requires (legal obligation).
To look after our business, for example to deal with a complaint or a claim (our legitimate interests).
We only send you news or offers if you have asked for them, and you can stop them at any time. We never sell your personal data.

Only those who need it: your host, the landlords of your home, and the coworking, insurance, language-school and vehicle providers you choose as add-ons, and the companies that provide our email, form handling and website hosting. Each receives only what it needs. We may also share data where the law requires it.

Your trip takes place outside the country where you may live, so the people delivering it will receive the details they need there. Where the law requires it, we put appropriate safeguards in place for those transfers, such as contractual commitments, or rely on the transfer being necessary to arrange the trip you asked for. You can ask us about them.

Enquiries that do not lead to a booking are deleted within two years of our last contact. Booking records are kept for as long as tax and accounting law requires, and then deleted. Health and access details are deleted once your trip is over, unless you ask us to keep them for a future trip.
We keep personal data in secure, access-controlled systems and share it only as described here. If something goes wrong that affects your data, we will tell you.

You can ask us for a copy of your personal data, and ask us to correct it, delete it, limit how we use it, or send it to you or someone else in a portable form. You can object to our using it on the basis of our legitimate interests, and withdraw any consent you have given. Write to
; we reply within one month. If you are not happy with our answer, you can complain to the data protection authority in the country where you live or work.
We update this policy when our practices change. The date at the top shows the latest version.
The booking terms for a Sabbatical long-stay package.
The terms for a long stay planned with us, from first inquiry to coming home.

These terms apply to every trip arranged by Sabbatical (“we”, “us”), Second Home Lisboa, Mercado da Ribeira, Avenida 24 de Julho 49, 1200-479 Lisboa, Portugal, and to your use of this website. Please read them before you book. “You” means everyone travelling on the booking; the person who makes the booking accepts these terms for the whole group.

Sending an enquiry is free and commits you to nothing. We reply with questions, then a written proposal built for your dates, group and route. Prices shown on this site are guides (“from”) and are not offers; the price of your trip, what it includes and how long the proposal stays open are set out in the proposal. Prices depend on availability until the booking is confirmed.

A booking is made when you accept a proposal in writing and pay the deposit stated in it, and we confirm the booking in writing. Your confirmation sets out the trip, the price and the date the balance is due. Please check it and tell us straight away if anything is wrong, including names, which must match your passports.

A deposit is due when you book and the balance is due before you travel, on the date set out in your proposal and confirmation. If the balance is not paid on time, we may treat the booking as cancelled by you, and the cancellation charges below apply.

We will try to help if you want to change a confirmed booking, but cannot promise to. Changes may carry a cost, including charges from camps, hotels, airlines and other suppliers, and we will tell you what it is before you decide.

You can cancel at any time by writing to us. Cancellation charges then apply: they increase as the travel date gets closer and reflect the costs we and our suppliers cannot recover. The charges for your trip are set out in your proposal and confirmation. Your travel insurance may cover them.
If we change or cancel your trip

Tailor-made travel sometimes needs adjusting. If we have to make a significant change to your trip before you travel, we will tell you as soon as possible and offer you the choice of accepting the change, taking a comparable alternative, or cancelling with a full refund of what you have paid us. We will not cancel your trip after the balance is paid except for reasons beyond our control, and if we do, we will refund what you have paid us.

We are not responsible for changes, delays or cancellations caused by events that neither we nor our suppliers could foresee or avoid, such as extreme weather, natural disasters, epidemics, civil unrest, strikes, or official advice against travel. If such an event stops your trip, we will refund what we can recover and help you rearrange.

You must have travel insurance that covers cancellation, medical treatment, repatriation and the activities in your trip, from the moment you book. Please send us the policy details before you travel.

You are responsible for a valid passport, any visa you need, the vaccinations and health documents required, and for meeting the entry rules of every country you pass through. We give general information in good faith, but rules change: always check them with official sources and your doctor before you travel.

Please follow the reasonable instructions of the people looking after you, respect local laws and customs, and tell us before you book about any medical condition, disability or needs that may affect your trip, so we can check that it suits you.

We will plan and arrange your trip with reasonable skill and care and are responsible for making sure the arrangements we confirm are provided. We are not responsible where a problem is caused by you, by someone unconnected with your trip, or by events beyond anyone’s control. Where international conventions limit the liability of airlines, other carriers or hotels, our liability is limited in the same way. Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or anything else that cannot be limited by law.
If you have a problem during your trip, tell the person looking after you and contact us straight away, so we can try to put it right on the spot. If you are still unhappy, write to
within 28 days of coming home; we will reply within 28 days.

We describe places, seasons and entry rules as carefully as we can, but these change. The text and design of this site belong to us; photographs belong to their owners and are used with permission or under their licences. We link to other sites for information and are not responsible for their content.

These terms are governed by the law that applies where Sabbatical is established, and disputes go to the courts there. This does not take away any rights you have under the consumer law of the country where you live.
